concepts.title: Permanent Settlement and Zamindars
concepts.definition: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 fixed Bengal's revenue demand forever and made zamindars proprietors answerable for payment by sunset on fixed dates; default brought auction of their estates, so the East Company's state shifted risk onto the rural elite.
concepts.key_idea: Fixed demand plus strict sunset rules were designed for predictability, but fluctuating harvests made zamindars the first losers.

concepts.title: Jotedars and Rural Power
concepts.definition: Within Bengal villages, jotedars - rich peasants holding substantial land - controlled local credit, leased land to under-ryots and resisted zamindar demands far more effectively than zamindars resisted the state, shifting real rural power below the proprietors.
concepts.key_idea: While zamindars urbanised and defaulted, jotedars stayed in the village, buying auctioned land and tightening their grip on tenants.

solution_steps.explain: jotedars held land and money-lending power over under-ryots

concepts.title: Santhals and the Rajmahal Hills
concepts.definition: The Santhals migrated into the Rajmahal hills from the late eighteenth century, clearing forests for settled cultivation, clashing with Paharia herdsmen, and eventually rebelling in 1855-56 against moneylenders, indigo planters and colonial officials, which led to the creation of a separate Santhal district.
concepts.key_idea: Santhal settlement turned forest into paddy land, but traders' debts and state taxes converted gratitude into the great rebellion.

concepts.title: Deccan Riots and the Cotton Boom
concepts.definition: The American Civil War cotton boom (1860s) drew Deccan ryots into credit-financed cotton exports; when prices crashed after 1864, debt to sahukars crushed peasants, and in 1875 ryots attacked moneylenders' houses and account books, prompting the Deccan Riots Commission.
concepts.key_idea: The rioters targeted the bahi khatas - account books - showing that the battle was over debt records as much as grain.

concepts.title: Colonial Countryside Timeline
concepts.definition: Key countryside dates form a chain: the Permanent Settlement in 1793, the Santhal rebellion in 1855, and the Deccan riots in 1875; each interval is found by subtracting the earlier year from the later one.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the settlement year from the Santhal year measures how long the settlement's order lasted before open rebellion.
